newsitem.title: UK: Bagri, Rowlands head UK businessmen honoured.
newsitem.headline: Bagri, Rowlands head UK businessmen honoured.

text.p: The chairman of the London Metal Exchange (LME) was given a life peerage on Tuesday in Britain's New Year's Honours list, which also featured knighthoods for David Rowlands and Robert Horton.
Indian-born Raj Bagri, 66, has been chairman of the LME since 1993 and the peerage will enable him to sit in Parliament's House of Lords upper house.
Rowlands, chairman of Lloyd's insurance market, said his knighthood recognised the efforts of "many, many people" to complete the reconstruction of Lloyd's.
Horton is head of the privatised Railtrack.

Other business and industry figures given knighthoods include Peter Davies, chief executive of Prudential Corp, Michael Pickard, chairman of the London Docklands Development Corporation; John Laing, chairman of construction group John Laing Plc and Brian Richards, co-founder of British Biotech Plc.
